# {{displayName}}

{{description}}

A [Breezell](https://breezell.com) plugin (`{{id}}`).

## Develop

```bash
npm install
```

Open this folder in Breezell and press **F5**: the plugin runs in a development window.
Plugins run only while you are signed in to Breezell.

- `src/extension.ts` — the plugin. Besides the VS Code API it can use `vscode.breezell`
  (typings in `types/breezell.d.ts`); ask only for the permissions you need in
  `package.json` › `breezell.permissions`.
- `npm run validate` — check `package.json`.

## Package

```bash
npm run package:open     # open source: the source ships in the package
npm run package:closed   # closed source: minified build only, no source
```

Either command writes `{{id}}-<version>.vsix`. Install it in Breezell from
**Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix**. It works without uploading it anywhere.

## Publish to the Breezell plugin market

1. Fork [BreezellCode/BreezellCode](https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode) and clone your fork.
2. `node tools/breezell-plugin.mjs submit --market <path to your clone>`
3. Commit, push and open a pull request. The market check runs on it.

Guide: <https://github.com/BreezellCode/BreezellCode/tree/main/plugins>

# {{displayName}}

{{description}}

A Breezell plugin pack (`{{id}}`): no code, only what `package.json` › `contributes.breezell` declares.

- `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`: skills the agent can load (they show up in Breezell's skill list).
- `rules/rules.md`: rules added to the AI's instructions while the pack is on.
- `mcpServers`: MCP servers, e.g. `"thinking": { "command": "npx", "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-sequential-thinking"] }`.
  Users see the command before they install.
- `contributes.themes`: color themes, as in any VS Code extension.

```bash
npm run validate
npm run package:open      # writes {{id}}-<version>.vsix
```

Install the .vsix in Breezell from **Plugins › Installed › Install local .vsix**, or press F5 to try the pack in a development window.

     installed and on. Keep them short: they count against every request. -->
- Before editing several files, say in one sentence what you are going to change.

name: example-skill
description: Describe when the agent should use this skill, in one sentence. The agent reads this line to decide.

# Example skill

Steps the agent follows when it uses this skill. Keep them short and concrete:

1. What to look at first.
2. What to do.
3. How to check the result.

Put more skills next to this folder: `skills/<skill-name>/SKILL.md`.
